title: Armenia just opened the region’s biggest AI factory. It exists because Washington signed a licence.
excerpt: Firebird opened the CIS region's largest AI factory in Armenia. The GPU count matters less than the export licence and the Kazakh minister in the room.
content_html:
Firebird, a US-based AI cloud company, opened what NVIDIA calls the CIS region’s largest AI factory in Hrazdan, Armenia on Saturday. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan attended, alongside Kazakhstan’s deputy prime minister Zhaslan Madiyev and David Allen, the US chargé d’affaires in Armenia.

That guest list is the story. A US company opened a facility in a country inside Russia’s traditional sphere of influence, with an American diplomat and a Kazakh minister watching.

The licence is the load-bearing fact

None of this happens without export approval. Firebird secured a US export licence in November 2025, the regulatory step that allowed advanced NVIDIA hardware into Armenia at all.

The politics were made explicit in February. Firebird and the US government jointly announced Phase 2 at a Yerevan press conference during Vice President JD Vance’s visit, scaling the project to $4 billion and roughly 50,000 GPUs with licensing for a further 41,000 NVIDIA GB300 units.

Phase One was $500 million. The announcement claimed Armenia would host one of the world’s five largest AI GPU clusters.

What is actually running

The opened flagship, DC-1, is specified at 6,144 NVIDIA B200 GPUs across 15 megawatts, liquid-cooled and built on NVIDIA’s reference architecture. The target is more than 70,000 Rubin and Blackwell GPUs and 300 megawatts by the end of 2027.

That is a twentyfold increase in power capacity in roughly 17 months. A planned DC-2 is listed at 75,000 VR200 GPUs across 125 megawatts, with a third site at similar scale.

The delivery speed is genuinely notable. NVIDIA says the site went from plan to operating capacity in just over six months, with Schneider Electric supplying switchgear, three-phase UPS systems and rack enclosures, and Vertiv providing chilled-water cooling.

The power trick

The facility runs on NVIDIA’s DSX platform, which codesigns compute, networking, power and cooling as a single system rather than separate procurements. NVIDIA claims it allows up to 40% more GPUs on the same footprint by recovering stranded power.

For a site scaling from 15 to 300 megawatts, that coordination is where the capacity maths gets made. It is also, in NVIDIA’s own framing, a tokens-per-dollar argument rather than a performance one.

Who is paying for it

Firebird said NVIDIA intends to invest in the company, following an earlier CoreWeave investment this year. The pattern is familiar: NVIDIA takes a position in a company that then buys NVIDIA hardware at scale.

NVIDIA has now committed more than $40 billion to AI equity positions in 2026, and the structures have grown more creative. It took a $2.1 billion warrant in IREN as part of a five-gigawatt data centre deal.

The same logic runs through its sovereign deals. NVIDIA invested $1 billion in Naver while striking a $500 billion arrangement with SK Group, an approach critics have labelled circular financing.

The neocloud playbook

Firebird fits a category that barely existed three years ago: companies that buy GPUs at scale and rent them to model builders. CoreWeave, an early Firebird backer, has signed a multi-year deal with Anthropic to run Claude at production scale.

Europe has its own version. Nscale committed €695 million to Portugal with Microsoft, reaching a $14.6 billion valuation in two years, on much the same thesis about sovereign capacity.

Firebird’s first named customer is Perplexity, which is using the site for its answer engine and AI agent platform.

Where this goes next

Firebird is pursuing an approximately two-gigawatt roadmap spanning Armenia, Kazakhstan and further markets, which explains why a Kazakh deputy prime minister was at an Armenian ribbon-cutting.

The strategic logic is straightforward. Compute is becoming the thing countries align around, and the United States has found a way to place it in a region where its influence has historically been thin.

The open question is demand. Building 300 megawatts in the Caucasus assumes customers will route workloads there rather than to cheaper or closer capacity, and one answer engine does not settle that.

content_html_zh:
总部位于美国的 AI 云公司 Firebird 于周六在亚美尼亚赫拉兹丹开设了 NVIDIA 称之为独联体地区最大的 AI 工厂。 亚美尼亚总理尼科尔·帕希尼扬、哈萨克斯坦副总理扎斯兰·马季耶夫和美国驻亚美尼亚临时代办戴维·艾伦出席。

宾客名单就是故事。 一家美国公司在俄罗斯传统势力范围内的一个国家开设了一家工厂，一名美国外交官和一名哈萨克斯坦部长在场观看。

许可证是承重事实

如果没有出口批准，这一切都不会发生。 Firebird 于 2025 年 11 月获得美国出口许可证，这一监管步骤允许先进的 NVIDIA 硬件进入亚美尼亚。

政治在二月份就已经明确了。 Firebird 和美国政府在副总统 JD Vance 访问埃里温期间举行的新闻发布会上联合宣布了第二阶段计划，将该项目规模扩大到 40 亿美元，配备约 50,000 个 GPU，并获得另外 41,000 个 NVIDIA GB300 单元的许可。

第一阶段耗资 5 亿美元。 该公告称，亚美尼亚将拥有世界上五个最大的 AI GPU 集群之一。

实际运行的是什么

开放的旗舰产品 DC-1 配备 6,144 个 NVIDIA B200 GPU，功率达 15 兆瓦，液冷，基于 NVIDIA 参考架构构建。 目标是到 2027 年底拥有超过 70,000 个 Rubin 和 Blackwell GPU 以及 300 兆瓦。

这意味着电力容量在大约 17 个月内增加了 20 倍。 计划中的 DC-2 预计配备 75,000 个 VR200 GPU，功率达 125 兆瓦，第三个站点也具有类似规模。

交货速度确实值得注意。 NVIDIA 表示，该站点从计划到投入运营仅用了六个多月的时间，施耐德电气提供开关设备、三相 UPS 系统和机架外壳，维谛技术 (Vertiv) 提供冷冻水冷却。

力量技巧

该设施在 NVIDIA 的 DSX 平台上运行，该平台将计算、网络、电源和冷却系统共同设计为一个系统，而不是单独采购。 NVIDIA 声称，通过恢复闲置电源，可以在相同的占地面积上增加多达 40% 的 GPU。

对于容量从 15 兆瓦到 300 兆瓦的站点，这种协调就是进行容量数学计算的地方。 在 NVIDIA 自己的框架中，这也是一种每美元代币的争论，而不是性能的争论。

谁为此付出代价

Firebird 表示，继今年早些时候对 CoreWeave 进行投资后，NVIDIA 打算投资该公司。 这种模式很熟悉：NVIDIA 在一家公司中占据一席之地，然后该公司大​​规模购买 NVIDIA 硬件。

NVIDIA 目前已承诺到 2026 年投资超过 400 亿美元的 AI 股权，而且结构也变得更具创意。 作为 5 吉瓦数据中心交易的一部分，它获得了 IREN 价值 21 亿美元的认股权证。

同样的逻辑也贯穿于其主权交易中。 NVIDIA 向 Naver 投资了 10 亿美元，同时与 SK 集团达成了 5000 亿美元的协议，批评者将这种做法称为循环融资。

Neocloud 剧本

Firebird 适合三年前几乎不存在的类别：大规模购买 GPU 并将其出租给模型构建者的公司。 CoreWeave 是 Firebird 的早期支持者，已与 Anthropic 签署了一份多年协议，以生产规模运行 Claude。

欧洲有自己的版本。 Nscale 与微软共同向葡萄牙投资 6.95 亿欧元，两年内估值达到 146 亿美元，其主权能力的论点与此基本相同。
